source.title: Better NTK Conditioning: A Free Lunch from (ReLU) Nonlinear Activation in Wide Neural Networks
source.authors: Chaoyue Liu; Han Bi; Like Hui; Xiao Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study trains wide ReLU networks at multiple depths and reports training-loss convergence, but it does not test the specific conditions or outcomes named by any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports initialization-time gradient angles and NTK condition numbers, which are not training-error outcomes. Its MNIST test-accuracy table measures generalization, not training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study reports depth-dependent convergence in fully connected ReLU networks, but tests none of V1–V6: it does not compare initialization schemes, residual shortcuts or normalization, measure the specified training-error or spurious-minimum outcomes, or examine learning-rate stability thresholds. Initialization-time gradient angles and NTK conditioning measure different constructs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that ReLU improves separation of similar inputs in gradient-feature space and NTK conditioning, with depth amplifying these effects. They connect conditioning to theoretical worst-case convergence rates and report faster convergence for deeper networks experimentally. MNIST test accuracy declines from 97.57% at depth 6 to 97.19% at depth 12, suggesting an optimization–generalization trade-off.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains fully connected 512-wide ReLU networks of depths 1–10 with cross-entropy and mini-batch SGD on MNIST, FashionMNIST, and Librispeech; it does not test the listed claim recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Network depth changes the reported training-loss convergence speed; deeper ReLU networks are described as converging faster than shallower ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5 and Figure 4 report faster training-loss convergence with increasing depth from 1 to 10 in 512-wide fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST, FashionMNIST and Librispeech, using grid-searched learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth can accelerate training-loss convergence in wide fully connected ReLU networks under NTK initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 reports greater minimum gradient-feature angles and smaller initialization-time NTK condition numbers for ReLU networks than corresponding linear networks, with stronger effects at greater depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ReLU activation and additional depth improve gradient-feature separation and NTK conditioning at initialization in the tested wide networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix B varies initialization variance from 0.01 to 10 and reports gradient-feature separation, without measuring learning speed or trainable depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-feature separation of similar inputs persists across the tested initialization scales.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, as stated in the text)
record.problems: Training-loss curves are figure-only in the supplied text, without extractable numeric values. The paper does not report training classification error or demonstrate convergence to zero error in these experiments.
record.rows_left_out: None; the separate depth-by-dataset training-loss curves are included. The MNIST test-accuracy results in Table 1 are omitted because they measure generalization rather than training error or convergence.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and size, stopping and regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student realizability, spurious local minima, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and prevention by identity shortcuts; special tanh initialization and Fixup.
Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth, signal and gradient preservation, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Normalization-dependent training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Faster convergence at depths 1–10 in fully connected networks does not challenge V3's depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks. A single initialization recipe does not test V4. The supplied figure text does not permit reliable numerical curve extraction; this is not evidence of a partial effect.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, training classification error, and the listed model-size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, batch normalization, and the listed depth, dataset, and initialization comparisons.
Comparisons among initialization schemes and trainability across the specified depths.
Learning rates relative to a stability threshold, loss-rise and curvature dynamics, sharpness, and divergence conditions.
Batch-normalized versus unnormalized training and the Fixup recipe.
